chunks: Yūnus, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
Those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except al-lamam.
He said: “The immoralities are adultery and theft; and al-lamam is that a man falls into a sin, then seeks Allah’s forgiveness for it.”
I said: “Is there a station between misguidance and kufr?” He said: “How many the bonds of īmān are!”

key_terms.اللَّمَمَ: a lesser lapse in which a person falls into sin and then seeks forgiveness
key_terms.الْفَوَاحِشَ: grave immoral acts, here explained as adultery and theft
key_terms.عُرَى الْإِيمَانِ: the bonds or branches of faith

ai.seo_question: What does al-lamam mean in Qur’an 53:32 according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur’anic phrase about avoiding major sins and immoralities except al-lamam. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام identifies grave immoralities such as adultery and theft, and defines al-lamam as a sin a person falls into and then seeks forgiveness from Allah for. It also indicates that states of belief are not reduced to a simple binary, but have many degrees and bonds within īmān.
